holidays.name: National Compliment Your Mirror Day
holidays.description: Give your mirror some love today. Tell that reflection it looks fantastic, even if your hair is doing something wild. It's a small dose of self-confidence, and it gives you a reason to start the day with a smile.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a staple of the quirky holiday calendar as a playful nudge toward self-kindness.
holidays.funFact: People have used mirrors for thousands of years. Some of the earliest were pieces of polished obsidian made in Anatolia (modern-day Turkey) around 6000 BCE.

holidays.name: National Eat Your Beans Day
holidays.description: Beans get a day in the spotlight. Chili, baked beans, burritos, hummus and three-bean salad are all fair game. Beans are cheap, filling, and full of fiber and plant protein.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It fits the summer cookout season, when baked beans are a barbecue classic.
holidays.funFact: Beans are one of the oldest cultivated crops. Humans have been growing them for thousands of years, and they are a dietary staple on nearly every continent.

holidays.name: National Fried Clam Day
holidays.description: Crispy, golden and a little messy, fried clams are a beloved seaside treat. Today is a good day to head to a clam shack, grab a paper boat of them with tartar sauce and a lemon wedge, and eat them with your fingers.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It celebrates a New England coastal tradition that is especially popular at summer clam shacks.
holidays.funFact: Fried clams are widely credited to Essex, Massachusetts. Lawrence "Chubby" Woodman is said to have fried the first batch there in 1916.
